It should be confirmed before the dry run: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/managing-billing-for-your-products/managing-billing-for-github-actions/about-billing-for-github-actions

- a brand mailbox the agent can SEND from (proposed step 8 is not done);

The arithmetic holds: $3,000 × 4 a year / 12 = $1,000 a month, × ₪3.6 = ₪3,600. The inputs do not hold.

(2) The timing makes 4 impossible within month 12. By the scout's own chain, the first filing is no earlier than about January 2027: a 30-day dry run, then owner steps 8 and 11, then filing. Each award then waits for triage, a fix and a Bounty Committee decision. At most one or two awards can land in the trailing year at September 2027.

(3) Averaging a lumpy award into a monthly figure breaks a standing rule:
- 'Prizes are not revenue' (docs/REJECTED.md:515).
- 'a ₪90,000 grant that lands once is a cash event, not an income line' (docs/REJECTED.md:501-502).

(5) The pool is crowded. Frontier labs mine the same surface, Mozilla's internal fuzzers have a 7-day window, and duplicates within 48 h split the award.

The dry run has not been run (logs/CHANNEL_LOOP.md:122).

estimate_basis:
INFERENCE with no base rate. The high case assumes at most one sec-high award (up to $3,000, a discretionary ceiling since bedrock PR #17331 of 18.8.2026) lands in the trailing 12 months at month 12 (September 2027). Averaged, that is $250 a month. At ₪3.6/USD (not measured) it is about ₪900 a month.

Timing bounds it. By the scout's own chain, filing starts no earlier than about January 2027, and each award then waits for triage, a fix and a committee decision.

The low case is ₪0. That result is at least as likely: the 30-day dry run has not been run; frontier labs are credited in 2026 advisories; Mozilla's fuzzers get a 7-day window; the collision window is now 48 h; and Mozilla is removing paid categories because 'AI makes it easier' (PR #17274, PR #17377).

The scout's ₪3,600 high multiplies correctly, but it assumes an invented four awards a year and is not reachable by month 12. Under docs/REJECTED.md:501-502 and :515 ('prizes are not revenue'), and BOARD-2.md:129-131, the portfolio should count this line at ₪0 a month in any case.

Discovery does not need a prior sale: there is no ranking or reputation gate. Reputation works only against us, through account disablement and reduced payouts for invalid reports.
honesty_risk:
The honesty risks are concrete.

(1) AI slop and invalid volume. An agent that files unreproduced or duplicate crashes is exactly what Mozilla penalises: accounts auto-disabled for too many Invalid bugs, and reduced payouts on the valid ones (bug-bounty.html). curl shut its bounty over 20 AI non-vulnerabilities in 21 days (docs/REJECTED.md:519). This needs a hard reproduce-and-minimise gate, a cap of perhaps one filing per verified finding, and a kill on the first Invalid cluster (KILL-3).

(2) Accountability. The BMO etiquette clause (added 23.4.2026) makes 'the person submitting' responsible and requires reports to 'reflect the reporter's own understanding'. On a brand account the accountable human is the owner, who cannot verify anything. AI disclosure is necessary but may not be sufficient; the Fable board must rule on this, as the screen did for Google's 'yourself' clause.

(3) Claiming for work the buyer has said it no longer needs. Mozilla removed the static-analysis bounty and the mitigation-analysis guidance in 2026 because AI makes them cheap. Filing AI-generated reports in those removed categories to fish for discretionary payouts would be dishonest.

(4) Disclosure harm. The most dangerous failure is a REST filing without the security group, or fuzz output committed to the public automaton repo. Either would leak an unfixed Firefox 0-day. This is an irreversible harm to users, not a terms issue.

(5) Identity. The credit can be the brand, but the payee's legal identity must not be hidden at payment. If payouts route via HackerOne, a Veriff selfie is likely, and that is a mandate violation (KILL-4).

(6) The breadth directive. Counting a lumpy discretionary award as monthly income would overstate the portfolio. This is the same honesty failure the 3.9 audit corrected (docs/REJECTED.md:501-502).

On the documented text this holds. monthly-payouts.mdx asks an individual for the legal full name and 'a clear, high-resolution photo of your ID card or driver's license'. It names no selfie, liveness check or video. A GitHub code search of apify/apify-docs for 'selfie OR liveness' returns 0 hits. Publishing needs no click. apify-api/openapi/paths/actors/acts@{actorId}.yaml says verbatim: 'To make your Actor public: Set `isPublic` to `true`. Provide `title` and `categories`.' So PUBLISH.md:39 and README.md step 3 do overstate the owner's work. Support is a different matter. Store Terms §8.1 require each user Issue to be addressed 'no later than within 14 days'. §8.2 requires an answer to Apify's direct requests within three business days. Under §7.1, an Actor that stays faulty for 30 days may be deprecated or removed. The public API has no Issues endpoint: the openapi/paths tree has 14 directories and actors/ has 40 files, none for issues. So support work grows with the fleet, and it looks Console-only, which means either the owner logs in and talks to customers (a mandate breach) or issues lapse. Whether an agent can handle issues without the owner's login is UNKNOWN.

The Store Publishing Terms have no clause on AI-generated or automated content. They forbid copying another creator's code or README (§2.2.3), off-platform promotion (§2.2.4.2(i)) and review manipulation, and Apify may unpublish at its discretion. The terms themselves pass. The median of 2 and '85% have ≥1 user' therefore describe Actors that passed it. A '1 user' Actor also typically logs about 29 runs (the daily test plus one account), consistent with that one user being the developer. (3) Two independent creator reports on GitHub, both third-party self-reports. williamcachamwri/wica, 17.8.2026: '23 of them live' from a new account, hidden from anonymous Store search with Console showing 'Identity verification required', and 'Real numbers after 89 days: 1 active user across all 23 tools. $0 revenue.' eltociear.github.io, 1.9.2026: 4 Actors, KYC 'approved', LIMITED_PERMISSIONS, still filtered from REST Store search yet ranked #2 on mcp.apify.com search-actors: 'Distinct users in 90 days: still 1, and that 1 is me', and 'Being findable turned out to be necessary and nowhere near sufficient.' (1) Self-referral, §6.1(v): a colony test sign-up, or the owner's friends or family signing up through our Store page or badge, breaches the terms, and §9 forfeits ALL commissions. CI must never create Apify accounts. (2) Promotion in Apify-owned content, §6.1(vi) plus Store Publishing Terms §2.2.4.2(i) (REJECTED.md:479-486): the Store README must not steer visitors to the GitHub repo or its referral badge. The badges must wait for the brand GitHub org (step 7), because the current public repo shows the owner's name.
